original_title: 10 Underrated TV Shows Based On Video Games
summary_en: Beyond the blockbusters like The Last of Us, a treasure trove of smaller-scale yet brilliant video game adaptations deserve your attention. Dive into these underappreciated gems that prove gaming's narrative power translates perfectly to the screen.
ai_analysis: This list offers a curated journey for dedicated series fans, highlighting adaptations that masterfully capture the essence of their source material beyond the obvious hits.

en.title: 7 Stellar TV Shows Based On Video Games You Might Have Missed
en.summary: Beyond the blockbusters like The Last of Us, a treasure trove of smaller-scale yet brilliant video game adaptations deserve your attention. Dive into these underappreciated gems that prove gaming's narrative power translates perfectly to the screen.
en.body:
## 1. Arcane: League of Legends
This animated series isn't just for League of Legends fans; it's a masterclass in character-driven storytelling set in a stunningly realized world of magic and technology. The breathtaking animation by Fortiche Production brings the complex relationship between sisters Vi and Jinx to life with emotional depth and spectacular action, making it a must-watch for anyone who appreciates rich lore and compelling drama.

## 2. Castlevania
Forget brooding vampires; this animated series reinvents the classic Konami franchise with sharp writing, visceral action, and surprisingly complex characters. Led by the brilliant mind of writer Warren Ellis, it transforms Dracula's war against humanity into a saga of loss, vengeance, and unlikely alliances, featuring some of the most fluid and brutal fight choreography ever animated.

## 3. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
While a new season of Cyberpunk is on the horizon for 2026, this standalone anime from Studio Trigger is a vibrant, high-octane dive into the neon-drenched, dystopian world of Night City. It tells a self-contained, tragic story of a street kid trying to survive the brutal cybernetic future, packed with Trigger's signature kinetic animation and emotional punch.

## 4. The Witcher: Blood Origin
Serving as a prequel to the main series, this limited series delves into the often-untold history of the Continent, exploring the Conjunction of the Spheres and the creation of the first Witcher. Despite its controversial reception, it offers a glimpse into a foundational moment of the Witcher universe, expanding the lore for dedicated fans eager to understand the origins of their favorite monster hunters.

## 5. Dota: Dragon's Blood
This Netflix animated series surprisingly delivers a mature and engaging fantasy narrative, expanding on the lore of Dota 2 with a focus on the dragon knight Davion and the princess Mirana. The intricate world-building and detailed character arcs, brought to life by the talented team at Studio Mir, make it a compelling watch even for those unfamiliar with the MOBA's complex universe.

## 6. Gears of War: The Series (Hypothetical)
While not yet a reality, the potential for a live-action Gears of War series is immense, given the franchise's rich lore and iconic characters like Marcus Fenix. Imagine the gritty, desperate battles against the Locust Horde brought to life with modern cinematic techniques, exploring themes of survival, sacrifice, and the cost of war on a truly epic scale.

## 7. Halo: Forward Unto Dawn
This live-action web series, released before the Paramount+ show, served as a crucial bridge, introducing viewers to the UNSC's struggle against the Covenant through the eyes of a young cadet. Its focus on character development and believable military sci-fi elements provided a grounded perspective on the Halo universe, offering a compelling narrative that complements the games' grander conflicts.
Bottom Line: Don't let these hidden gems slip through the cracks; these video game adaptations offer compelling stories and impressive craftsmanship worthy of any binge-watcher's queue.

content_raw: Everyone knows about Fallout and The Last of Us, but what about some of the more underrated TV shows based on video games?
